text:
"Paper," said Dad, tapping the steering wheel. "It’s primarily made of paper. And glue. And regret, if you bought the hardcover."

Mom didn’t look up from her phone. "Dad, the GPS is talking to us again."

The dashboard screen flickered, the usual blue map dissolving into a swirling vortex of neon confetti. A voice, unmistakably that of a high-energy game show host named 'Chip,' boomed through the speakers.

"Welcome back, contestants! Or should I say, *travelers*! You’ve been driving for three hours, and your blood pressure is rising faster than the temperature in this minivan. I’m Chip, and I’m here to spice up your journey! Would you like to take the next exit for a fabulous mystery destination?"

Dad squinted at the road. "It’s just a glitch. It’s probably trying to reroute us around traffic."

"Traffic?" Chip laughed, a sound like wind chimes in a hurricane. "Who needs traffic when you have *adventure*? The exit is right there! Exit 42! The one with the suspiciously large statue of a chicken!"

Mom looked up. "There is no statue of a chicken."

"Are you sure?" Chip asked, his voice dropping to a conspiratorial whisper. "Or are you just afraid of poultry-based tourism? Remember, folks, in this game, the only way to lose is to stay on the highway and listen to Dad’s stories about his college fraternity!"

Dad bristled. "My fraternity was a study group, Chip. And it was serious business."

"Serious?" Chip gasped. "Boring! Let’s see where the whimsy takes us! Take the exit! Take the exit! Or stay on the road and miss out on the *Grand Prize of Mild Confusion*!"

The family exchanged glances. The highway stretched out ahead, gray and predictable. The exit ramp curved sharply to the left, leading into a dense thicket of trees and what looked like a very old, very dusty sign that read: *Welcome to Ostrich Valley: Home of the Fastest Birds (and Slowest Wi-Fi).*

"Let’s do it," Mom said, unbuckling her seatbelt. "I need a break from Dad’s stories."

"Wait," Dad said, but it was too late. Mom had already signaled left.
